scope: Proposition 4.6 (Preliminary compactness) of the manuscript “The curve scaling limit of half-plane double dimers” (preprints/The-curve-scaling-limit-of-half-plane-double-dimers-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 226 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 2e1bcd39145db94c), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 23. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: The laws of F(Lδ) are tight in the collection space of closed-disk curves with the ensemble matching topology, with constant loops discarded. Moreover, the loops can be ordered by decreasing diameter and given measurable, orientation- preserving parametrizations whose joint laws are tight in the product of uniform path spaces. Every subsequential limit has finitely many loops above every positive diameter, and convergence retains all its nonconstant entries. At this stage limiting curves may be nonsimple, touch the boundary, or occur with multiplicity.
